source_text: Tantumque hoc prodigialis dogmatis nefas apostoli Pauli molitus est roborare sententiis, quas contextu totius lectionis exposui; et ostendi prophetam Isaiam, de quo hanc comparationem figuli constabat assumptam, iustitiae divinae plenissime causam tueri.
pass_a_gloss: And so great a crime of this monstrous dogma he has attempted to strengthen by sentences of the apostle Paul, which I have exposed by the context of the whole reading; and I have shown that the prophet Isaiah, from whom it stood this comparison of the potter was taken, most fully guards the cause of divine justice.
pass_b_english: He tried to strengthen this immense wickedness of a monstrous doctrine with statements of the apostle Paul, which I explained through the context of the entire passage. I also showed that the prophet Isaiah, from whom this potter comparison was admittedly taken, most fully defends the cause of divine justice (Isaiah 45:9) (Isaiah 29:16).

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Another Isaianic source for the potter analogy.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
